source: Orientation video for the Conversion Stories tab (ev-s7): nine testimonies (Strobel, Qureshi, Luckhoo, C.S. Lewis, Augustine, Pascal, Newton, J. Warner Wallace, Rosaria Butterfield). GUARDRAIL: a changed life is evidence of sincerity, NOT a proof of the resurrection — stated plainly. No unverified direct quotations. 'makes the case', never 'proves'. NOTE: scene 6 vo says 'Every argument across the Evidence Library' (adapted from the certified 'Every one of these arguments' — testimonies are not arguments).
voiceover: Some of the most formidable witnesses for the faith are people who set out to disprove it. This section tells nine of their stories. A legal journalist and a cold-case homicide detective each ran the evidence for the resurrection expecting to bury it — and were turned by it. And one of the world's most successful trial lawyers weighed it by the standard he used to win his cases, and judged it beyond reasonable doubt. C. S. Lewis came to belief reluctantly, against his own will. Augustine and Pascal each travelled a long road to deep conviction. John Newton, a slave trader, ended up writing Amazing Grace. A devout Muslim and a tenured professor each arrived where they never meant to go. A single changed life proves nothing on its own, and we don't pretend it does. But this many people, this unwilling, is a pattern worth reckoning with. Every argument across the Evidence Library gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. These are not proofs; they are evidence with a face — an invitation to look at what they saw. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
